headline: Functional oracles constrain pretrained genomic models for designed regulatory DNA
label: Constrained Nucleic Acid Generators
summary: Pretrained nucleotide models are being steered with functional oracles and RL to design regulatory DNA with controllable tissue specificity.
synthesis: The shared thread is steering pretrained nucleic acid generators with explicit functional objectives rather than retraining them from scratch. GENECraft is training-free, coupling a genomic language model with a functional oracle in a discrete dynamical system to design controllable regulatory DNA. REGAL instead uses reinforcement learning under sequence-to-function oracles to program enhancer regulatory grammar for tissue-specific design across species. GenNA differs in mechanism: it is a natural-language-guided autoregressive foundation model pretrained on a multimodal sequence-text corpus from 2221 eukaryotic species, conditioning nucleotide generation on textual annotations. What is new across these items is that the generative prior is paired either with an oracle that scores candidate sequences or with a conditioning channel that specifies the desired output. Only the first two items apply oracle-based constraints directly, so the dominant thread is oracle-guided control of pretrained DNA models.
